The knocking in the line had quit, which meant Tobin had won his argument with the valve. Maren set the bucket on the step and listened to the house settle around the new quiet.

She rinsed the clams twice and set them to purge. Outside, the tide was coming back, patient as anything, and the markers leaned with the first of an evening wind. Weather later, maybe. The sky had gone the color it goes before it changes its mind.

"Cream," she said to the empty kitchen, and wrote it on the slate by the door.

The heron went over the roof once, heading for the channel. She watched it out of sight, then put the kettle on, because the kettle was the answer to most of it.
